Purpose: Hero image for a post arguing that Beck's four rules of simple design remodel around intent, that duplicate expressions of intent invite divergence, and that documentation is becoming a derivative artifact generated from a single source of intent

Situation.Name: Subtraction
Situation.Setting: A dark, nearly empty workshop at night. On a long steel workbench stands ONE upright glowing crystalline record card, about the size of a tablet, showing six short labelled rows stacked vertically. From that single card, three thin beams of cyan light fan out and upward to three translucent holographic panes hanging in the air behind the bench: a documentation page, a test file, and a plain text guidance file. Each pane is clearly a projection of the card, not a separate document: same six rows visible faintly through each, rendered in a different layout. Nothing else is on the bench except two old hand-written paper copies of the same six rows, warm-grey and slightly crumpled, whose wording visibly differs from each other.
Situation.Camera: Wide mid-shot. Subject stands off-centre in the right third beside the bench, turned three-quarters toward camera. The glowing source card is at centre-left, the three projected panes fill the upper middle, with haze and negative space across the upper right for text overlay.

CharacterPose.Expression: Calm, decisive, a slight half-smile; the look of someone removing something that was never needed
CharacterPose.BodyPosition: Standing at the bench, weight settled, one hand resting flat near the glowing card
CharacterPose.Gesture: The other hand lifting one of the two paper copies up and away from the bench between finger and thumb, about to discard it
